result.title: Topic-Level Fairness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
result.summary: Group fairness in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems is typically evaluated using metrics aggregated across queries. However, such metrics can conceal topic-level disparities: a system may favor women on questions about human rights and men on questions about actors and filmmakers, appearing nearly neutral overall even though neither topic is fair. We therefore study topic-level fairness, which requires group fairness to hold within each topic rather than only in aggregate. To reduce the topic-level disparity, we adapt the reranker separately for each topic with a Bradley-Terry objective under direct supervision from the generated output: preference pairs built from the generator's own output carry the direction that topic requires. With preference pairs built from RoMQA alone, the adaptation reduces the mean absolute per-topic disparity by 51% on RoMQA and by 40% on TREC Fair Ranking while retaining accuracy. No baseline reaches the reduction, even when modified to treat each topic separately rather than apply one correction to every topic. Neither does our method with one reranker for all topics, which follows the direction that most topics require.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 RAG 系统中的主题级公平性，指出聚合指标会掩盖不同主题间的群体偏好差异，并提出按主题分别用 Bradley-Terry 目标微调 reranker，其偏好对由生成器自身输出构建，仅用 RoMQA 数据即可在保持准确率的同时显著降低主题间差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 非视觉、非 latent 推理工作，但「用生成器输出构造偏好对来直接监督上游筛选模块、并按主题分治」提供了下游信号回传训练证据选择器的线索，可供核查其在视觉证据筛选与贡献分配中的可迁移性。
